title: Acromioclavicular (AC) Joint Injury
case: Case: A 28-year-old cyclist fell onto the point of his left shoulder. Pain is localised to the AC joint and he has a small raised bump. Cross-body adduction is painful at the top of the shoulder. Passive elevation is limited by pain. No numbness, no breathing problems, normal pulses. X-ray shows mild AC separation without fracture.

Working diagnosis: AC joint sprain (grade II type). Plan: short-term sling for comfort, early pain-guided movement, scapular and cuff strengthening, avoid loading across the body early, progressive return to cycling and gym.

differentials.name: Clavicle fracture
differentials.key: Pain along the bone, bump, bruising, unable to lift arm

differentials.name: Sternoclavicular joint injury
differentials.key: Pain at the chest end of the collarbone
differentials.next: Medical review; urgent if airway or vascular symptoms

differentials.name: Biceps tendon pain
differentials.key: Anterior pain, tenderness over the groove

differentials.name: Distal clavicle osteolysis
differentials.key: Weightlifters with gradual pain and tenderness

qa: Why is a shoulder separation not the same as a shoulder dislocation? A separation affects the joint between the collarbone and shoulder blade, while a dislocation involves the ball and socket joint.
Why check along the whole clavicle? A fracture can look like an AC injury and needs different management.
Why avoid mobilising the AC joint? It is an injured, painful stabilising joint, and forcing it may increase pain and displacement.
Skin tenting over the bone end. What now? Refer urgently the same day because the skin is at risk.
The patient wants to know if surgery is needed. For types I and II conservative care is usual; higher grades need specialist input [Ref - to verify].

fields.Purpose: Compress the AC joint to see whether it reproduces pain
fields.Position: Sitting or standing; arm raised to 90 degrees forward flexion
fields.Action: Passively move the arm across the chest toward the opposite shoulder
fields.Positive: Pain located on top of the shoulder at the AC joint
fields.Negative: No pain, or pain located elsewhere such as the back of the shoulder (posterior capsule tightness)
fields.Supports: AC joint pain when combined with local tenderness
fields.Limits: Also painful in cuff and posterior shoulder conditions; interpret with location [Ref - to verify]

fields.Purpose: Help separate AC joint pain from deeper (labral or biceps anchor) pain
fields.Position: Standing; arm flexed to 90 degrees, adducted about 10 to 15 degrees, elbow straight
fields.Action: Step 1: arm internally rotated (thumb down); the therapist applies a downward force that the patient resists. Step 2: repeat with the palm up (arm externally rotated)
fields.Positive for AC joint: Pain on top of the shoulder in the thumb-down position that is reduced or gone with palm up
fields.Positive for deeper pain: Pain or clicking deep in the shoulder that is reduced with palm up
fields.Limits: Accuracy varies and the test is debated [Ref - to verify]

redFlags.Finding: Skin tenting or severely raised bone end
redFlags.Immediate action: Do not manipulate; refer same day

redFlags.Finding: Visible clavicle deformity, bruising along bone, cannot lift arm
redFlags.Immediate action: Support the arm; refer for imaging

redFlags.Finding: Hand numb, pale, cold, pulseless, or severe swelling
Chest pain, breathlessness, difficulty swallowing after trauma
Weight loss, constant night pain, cancer history

manual.name: Soft-tissue work around the shoulder (upper trapezius, pectoral)

manualNotes: Preferred starting choice: protection, pain control and early graded movement and strengthening. Manual therapy has little role in acute AC injury. Do not use techniques that stress the AC joint or force a displaced bone end.

exercise.Stage: 1: protect (type I to II: about the first days to weeks according to pain)
exercise.Exercise: Pendulum, pain-free elbow and hand movement, scapular setting
exercise.Steps: Support the arm; avoid lifting and cross-body positions
exercise.Starting dose: Short bouts, several times a day

exercise.Exercise: Isometric then banded rotation; rows; serratus punch
Overhead loading, push-ups, carries, sport drills
exercise.Progress when: Meets criteria for sport or work

exerciseNotes: Avoid early: heavy cross-body movements, bench press and push-up loads, direct blows and contact sport until pain and strength allow. No fixed time to return is stated; criteria are full range, near-normal strength, no pain with sport movements, and doctor clearance for contact sport [Ref - to verify].
A sling may be used for comfort for a short period. Long use is not recommended because it can lead to stiffness [Ref - to verify].
modalityNotes: Injections for AC osteoarthritis and surgery for higher grades are medical decisions.
pathway: Any emergency or urgent flag? Yes: act as in Section G.

Local AC tenderness, a fall onto the shoulder, painful cross-body test, no fracture signs? Yes: working diagnosis is AC joint sprain or separation. Ask a doctor for imaging when deformity is present or grading will change management.
Type I or II (minimal displacement)? Yes: conservative care.
Type III: shared decision between conservative care and surgery after specialist review [Ref - to verify].
Types IV to VI, skin compromise or neurovascular signs: urgent orthopaedic review.
Gradual onset and arthritis picture: manage as AC joint osteoarthritis or overuse.
Visit 1: screen flags, examine, refer for imaging if needed, protect and educate.
Early: pain control, short-term sling for comfort, early gentle movement.
